schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE INSURANCE (
    PID INT,
    TIV_2015 NUMERIC,
    TIV_2016 NUMERIC,
    LAT NUMERIC,
    LON NUMERIC,
    PRIMARY KEY (PID),
    CHECK (TIV_2015 >= 0),
    CHECK (TIV_2016 >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2: WITH T1 AS ( SELECT TIV_2015, 1 AS ISSATTIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(PID) >= 2 ), T2 AS ( SELECT LAT, LON, 1 AS ISUNIQUELOC FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT, LON HAVING COUNT(PID) = 1 ) SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE T3 LEFT JOIN T1 ON T3.TIV_2015 = T1.TIV_2015 LEFT JOIN T2 ON T3.LAT = T2.LAT AND T3.LON = T2.LON WHERE T1.ISSATTIV_2015 = 1 AND T2.ISUNIQUELOC = 1

q2_prompt_sql: WITH T1 AS ( SELECT TIV_2015, 1 AS ISSATTIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(PID) >= 2 ), T2 AS ( SELECT LAT, LON, 1 AS ISUNIQUELOC FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT, LON HAVING COUNT(PID) = 1 ) SELECT SUM(TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE T3 LEFT JOIN T1 ON T3.TIV_2015 = T1.TIV_2015 LEFT JOIN T2 ON T3.LAT = T2.LAT AND T3.LON = T2.LON WHERE T1.ISSATTIV_2015 = 1 AND T2.ISUNIQUELOC = 1
counterexample: INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (1, 1000, 500, 1.1, 2.2); INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (2, 1000, 600, 3.3, 4.4); INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (3, 1500, 700, 1.1, 2.2);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 incorrectly excludes policies with unique (LAT, LON) coordinates even if they have the same TIV_2015 as other policies. Q2 correctly identifies such policies by using a LEFT JOIN with a subquery that checks for unique (LAT, LON) coordinates.
counterexample_dsp: A test case where there are two policies with the same TIV_2015 but different (LAT, LON) coordinates, and another policy with the same (LAT, LON) coordinates but a different TIV_2015.
